4.0.0.en: Dim: lost its beauty, strength and splendor.

4.0.1.en: Most fine gold: pure gold. The prophet marvels at the ruin of the temple of God, built of great stones and overlaid with pure gold, and how the gold fell into the dust and lost its luster, and the stones of the temple walls were scattered in the streets around it. All this is the result of the Babylonian attack that destroyed the temple of Solomon.

4.1.0.en: The Babylonians did not only tear down the temple of God and break the gold in it, but also crushed the Jews who believed in God, who had great value among the peoples, for their value was like gold and better than it. These Jews were slain and fell wounded because of their departing from God and neglecting Him.

4.2.0.en: Jackals: an animal that lives in abandoned places, its size between that of the fox and the wolf.

4.2.1.en: Breasts: plural of breast, with which the female nurses her child.

4.2.3.en: Cruel: harsh. When the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem she became a ruin and was filled with wild and savage animals such as jackals, which take care to nurse their young; but Jerusalem, because of the Babylonian siege upon her, found no food with which to feed her children, so she left them to die, as the ostrich flees and leaves its eggs that it laid and prepared for in the dust, covering them with it, when it senses danger and flees from the hunters. That is, he represents Jerusalem as a mother who became harsh to her children and left them to die of hunger or by the sword of Babylon.

4.3.0.en: The prophet shows the cruelty of the hunger to which Jerusalem was exposed during Babylon's siege of her, and how the mouths of the infants dried up for lack of water. And the children ask their parents to give them bread, and the fathers find no bread to break and give small pieces of it to their children so that they may not die.

4.4.0.en: Scarlet: a dark red color, and what is meant is the scarlet garments worn by the great and the rich. He continues his description of the cruelty of the famine in Jerusalem, and the prophet says that the rich of Jerusalem, who used to eat sumptuous foods, found no bread or water in the time of hunger. They used to wear luxurious garments of scarlet, purple and other clothing of the wealthy, but now they have fallen in the streets in the dust, groaning and dying of hunger and thirst.

4.5.0.en: Punishment: chastisement. The prophet remembers the ruin of Sodom, which burned because of its evil, and says that the state of Jerusalem is harder than that of Sodom, for the enemy attacked her after besieging her and killed and wounded those in her, whereas the people of Sodom died without the hand of enemies; but in the case of Jerusalem, God used the hand of Babylon to discipline them severely, that perhaps they might repent.

4.5.1.en: Do not hate the one who troubles you, and do not murmur at trials, but accept them from the hand of God and remember your sins, for perhaps they are the cause, so you return to Him by repentance, and then He removes all your troubles from you and even rewards you with many blessings for your repentance and your supplication to Him.

4.6.0.en: Her Nazarites: persons who vow themselves to God for a certain period which they spend in fasting and prayer, so God gives them splendor and grace.

4.6.1.en: Rubies: a kind of precious stone, its color tending to red, found in the seas such as the Red Sea.

4.6.3.en: Like sapphire: a kind of precious stone, transparent, tending to blue and distinguished by hardness. He describes those who worship God in His holy temple in Jerusalem, who present themselves as Nazarites to God, and who were distinguished by purity like pure snow, and God gives them grace so their faces become white as milk, and they were full of vitality, and their bodies tended to redness like the stones of coral and like the sapphire, beautiful in appearance and tending to a light blue. That is, the Jews who believed in God enjoyed purity, vitality and whiteness, and the color red, which symbolizes love and self-giving, and the color blue, which symbolizes heaven. These who worshiped God perished by the hand of Babylon because they neglected their worship and were occupied with the worship of idols.

4.7.0.en: When Babylon attacked Jerusalem and destroyed the city, and its inhabitants fell wounded and slain by hunger and by the sword, their appearance became black like the darkness, and when they fell in the streets it was no longer easy to recognize them, because their appearance changed through hunger, for their bodies became very thin and their skin clung to their bones, and their flesh had vanished from weakness, and their appearance became like a dry piece of wood.

4.7.1.en: V. 9: The Jews who died by the sword of Babylon were in a better state than the Jews who were tormented by hunger, for they found no fruits of the field to eat because of the siege of Jerusalem, and in the end they died a very painful death.

4.8.0.en: The pitiful: plural of tender one, for the mother is distinguished by tenderness toward her children by the instinct of motherhood. Among the most horrible scenes that occurred in the famine in Jerusalem at Babylon's siege of her was that from intense hunger the mothers cooked their infant children and ate them.

4.9.0.en: Zion: an ancient name for Jerusalem. Thus God took care to discipline Jerusalem, and when His wrath came upon her, Babylon destroyed her and burned her temple and her palaces.

4.10.0.en: Because of the greatness of Jerusalem and the strength of her temple and the presence of God in it, the peoples around her were astonished at the attack of the Babylonian enemy upon her and her destruction.

4.10.1.en: [2] The destruction of Jerusalem because of her sins (vv. 13-20)

4.10.2.en: 13- For the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her, 14- They have wandered as blind men in the streets, they have polluted themselves with blood, so that men could not touch their garments. 15- They cried unto them, Depart ye; it is unclean; depart, depart, touch not: when they fled away and wandered, they said among the heathen, They shall no more sojourn there. 16- The anger of the LORD hath divided them; he will no more regard them: they respected not the persons of the priests, they favoured not the elders. 17- As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us. 18- They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets: our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end is come. 19- Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of the heaven: they pursued us upon the mountains, they laid wait for us in the wilderness. 20- The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD, was taken in their pits, of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the heathen.

4.11.0.en: The prophet makes clear the reason for the destruction of Jerusalem, which is the sins of her false prophets who led the people astray, and also the priests who condemned the innocent to death, such as their attempt to kill Jeremiah

4.12.0.en: He declares that the leaders of the Jewish people no longer see the truth, that is, God, that is, they became blind to the knowledge of God, and evil covered them, that is, they became guilty against God, and the blood of those whom they killed cries out before God, so they became more unclean than the lepers who go outside the cities and cry, Unclean, unclean, so that no one comes near them and touches them and becomes unclean.

4.13.0.en: He likens the leaders of the Jews at their flight from Jerusalem to the unclean lepers who live outside the inhabited cities, so that every person keeps away from them. In the same way the nations kept away from the fleeing Jews, lest the sword of Babylon strike them, and the nations felt that Jerusalem would not be inhabited afterward, because her ruin was great.

4.14.0.en: Hath divided them: scattered them. He makes clear that the Jews' flight was from God, who permitted Babylon to attack them, so they are scattered over the earth, whether by fleeing or by being taken captive by the Babylonians, and all this was because of their sins, for they did not honor the priests or the elders, but speech became for selfishness, evil and cruelty.

4.15.1.en: Jeremiah expresses the state of his people, who had allied with Egypt. When Babylon besieged Jerusalem, the Jews waited for help to come to them from Egypt but found none, and when the Jews hid in their towers and fortresses from the face of Babylon, they waited for Egypt to save them, but it did not come to them, to show the vanity of relying on men. It would have been better for them to trust in God alone, since the idol gods they worshiped did not help them.

4.15.2.en: Do not let your eyes be deceived by money or position or all the powers of the world, for they are worthless when God permits your discipline. Return to Him by repentance and you will obtain His mercies, and I wish you would not leave Him again, so that you are not exposed to these disciplines, and thank Him for His discipline because He loves you and seeks the salvation of your soul; if you do not understand from His gifts, He permits discipline.

4.16.0.en: Babylon attacked Jerusalem, so the Jews fled and hid in every corner, because the armies of Babylon set snares everywhere to seize the Jews and kill them. Thus the Jews lost their freedom of movement in their ways and the squares of the city.

4.17.0.en: Laid wait: hid. Pursued: hastened after them.

4.17.1.en: The Babylonian soldiers pursued the Jews everywhere, and when the Jews tried to flee, they hastened after them and overtook them, because they were extremely swift like the eagles, and even when the Jews went to hide in the mountains the Babylonians pursued them there, and in the wilderness the Babylonians hid to pounce on the Jews and seize them if they passed through the wilderness.

4.18.0.en: The breath of our nostrils: the most important person we have, who gives us life, because breathing is an essential process for life; the anointed of the Lord is likened to it.

4.18.1.en: Their pits: their snares with which they hunt us.

4.18.2.en: This is a clear prophecy about Christ when the Jews seized Him and delivered Him to be crucified. He was the hope of the people for delivering them from the Romans, and they found the Romans crucifying Him, and the Jews did not understand that He came to redeem them from sin and to die for them. This verse also applies to the king of Judah, Zedekiah, whom Babylon seized and killed his sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, and it applies also to all the chiefs of Judah and their prophets, and it applies also to Jeremiah, for Babylon seized all of them and killed some of them.

4.18.4.en: 21- Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, that dwellest in the land of Uz; the cup also shall pass through unto thee: thou shalt be drunken, and shalt make thyself naked.

4.18.5.en: 22- The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; he will no more carry thee away into captivity: he will visit thine iniquity, O daughter of Edom; he will discover thy sins.

4.19.0.en: God mocks the offspring of Edom, that is, the offspring of Esau, who dwell next to the children of Israel, south of the land of the Jews in the region of the mountains of Seir. He says to the land of Edom, mocking it, let it go on in its joy and merriment since it gloated over the fall of Jerusalem, and warns it that He will discipline it and it also will fall by the hand of Babylon, because it gloated over the calamity of its brothers the Jews.

4.19.1.en: If you see your brother meeting a problem and distress, pray for him and do not reproach him or gloat over him, for if you humble yourself before God, He will keep you and save you from distresses; and if your heart is filled with evil toward your brothers, know that God is just and will repay you for your evil.

4.20.0.en: God reassures His people when He calls her daughter of Zion, declaring that her discipline by captivity for her iniquities is accomplished and she will not be disciplined by other distresses; on the contrary, after a time the captivity will end and she will return to her land honored, and on the contrary, Edom, which gloated over her, will be punished for her sins and for her gloating. God saves His humiliated children

5.0.0.en: Behold: look out from the balcony.

5.0.1.en: The last chapter is a prayer more than a lament, in which he entreats God to look upon the bad state of His people and the shame into which they have come.

5.1.0.en: The first thing God notices, or Jeremiah asks of Him, is that He deliver them from the Babylonian occupation that seized their houses and fields and all that they own, and this is what Satan does with the one who is lax toward sin, for he robs him of his abilities.

5.2.0.en: After the men of the kingdom of Judah were killed, the children became orphans and their mothers widows, that is, they became weak, without strength, for the person who has fallen into sin has lost the power of God working in him, because he rejected God, so God abandoned him.

5.3.0.en: The Babylonian enemy pressed upon Jerusalem, besieged, or after she fell into their hands and they killed her men, so the necessities of life such as water were not available, and they bought it, because of its scarcity, at a high price which is expressed by silver, and even wood, that is, sticks of dry plants used for lighting fire, which is considered very cheap and without price; that is, the cost was extreme and the necessities of man were unavailable. This is what Satan does to keep us away from God, the source of our life, for the Holy Spirit is the spring of our water and the fire that burns our sins.

5.4.0.en: The Babylonians enslaved the people of God and put the yoke on their necks to work as forced labor, or beat them with staves on their necks and drove them out of their cities, and despite the work and much toil they did not obtain the necessary sustenance.

5.5.0.en: In the distress of hunger in which the Jews found themselves, they tried to ask help from Egypt or Assyria to obtain bread, that is, the necessities of life, but no one came to their aid, and it would have been better for them to take refuge in God and not trust in the arm of flesh. When they repented and returned to God, He brought them back from captivity.

5.6.0.en: Jeremiah confesses on behalf of the people that their fathers sinned by worshiping idols and evil lusts, and the discipline of the Lord came upon the sons, because they walked in the way of their fathers' sins, so they deserved punishment.

5.6.1.en: Do not give up your spiritual weapons and your food, which are Holy Communion, the word of God and prayer, lest Satan deprive you of them and you obtain them with difficulty afterward. Hold fast to your spiritual rule and compel yourself to it, for what you compel yourself to today you will become accustomed to and enjoy tomorrow.

5.6.3.en: 8- Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand. 9- We gat our bread with the peril of our lives because of the sword of the wilderness. 10- Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine. 11- They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in the cities of Judah. 12- Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured. 13- They took the young men to grind, and the children fell under the wood. 14- The elders have ceased from the gate, the young men from their musick. 15- The joy of our heart is ceased; our dance is turned into mourning. 16- The crown is fallen from our head: woe unto us, that we have sinned! 17- For this our heart is faint; for these things our eyes are dim. 18- Because of the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, the foxes walk upon it.

5.7.0.en: Jerusalem was a great city, and the people of God took pride in the presence of the temple in their midst, and they were exalted above all the peoples by their knowledge of God, but when they forsook God they grew weak, and those weaker than they, who were spiritually like slaves to them, gained dominion over them, so they became their chiefs and occupiers, and their occupation lasted long and none of the surrounding peoples delivered them, because God wanted to discipline them for 70 years, which is the duration of their captivity.

5.8.0.en: Because of the cruelty of the Babylonian occupation that controlled the streets of Jerusalem and the land of Judea, it became hard for the people of God to obtain their bread, that is, the necessary sustenance, so they used to seize the opportunity to gather some grains of wheat or barley or fruits of the field to satisfy their hunger.

5.9.0.en: Oven: a furnace. The hunger grew severe upon the people of God and lasted long, so their skin clung to their bones and even became dark, tending to black, as though their skins had been burned in an oven and become black.

5.10.0.en: The hand of the soldiers of Babylon reached out to assault and rape the virgin women of the people of God. So Satan humiliates the one who submits to him through evil lusts.

5.11.0.en: The Babylonian humiliation extended and tortured the people, especially their chiefs, whom they hanged up by their hands in the air, and the hand of torture reached the elders as well as the young.

5.11.1.en: Be careful of sin, whether you are a man or a woman, a young man or a young woman or in old age, for Satan exploits every opportunity to make you fall into sin. So guard against the sources of sin and keep away from them, and if you fall, repent quickly so that God may raise you up and you may trample the devil.

5.12.0.en: Babylon used the young men of the people of God for grinding, exploiting their strength instead of the women who used to grind at the mill, and as for the boys, they exploited them to work in the houses carrying wood and lighting fires, so they fell from intense exhaustion.

5.13.0.en: The elders were accustomed to sit at the gate of the city for judging and settling disputes, but after the ruin of the land they no longer sat in the square at the gate, and on the other hand the young men were in sorrow and no longer sang songs of joy. When a person is lax toward sin he loses his ability to discern and judge, and he also loses his joy.

5.14.0.en: Joy departed from the hearts of the people of God, and instead of expressing joy with dancing games they were weeping over the humiliation in which they found themselves.

5.15.0.en: Their glory was also lost, which is expressed by the crown they wear on their heads. All this is discipline from God because of our sins.

5.16.0.en: Hearts became sorrowful and eyes grew weak from much weeping, and this symbolizes the weakness of spiritual insight in sinners and their loss of peace and happiness

5.17.0.en: Jerusalem, built on five mountains, the most important of which is Mount Zion, became a ruin, and instead of her sons walking on these mountains she became deserted of people and foxes run in her.

5.17.2.en: 19- Thou, O LORD, remainest for ever; thy throne from generation to generation. 20- Wherefore dost thou forget us for ever, and forsake us so long time? 21- Turn thou us unto thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old. 22- Hast thou utterly rejected us? art thou very wroth against us?

5.18.0.en: The hearts of the people of God turn to Him in hope that He may deliver them from their humiliation, and they declare their faith in His power, for He is the King of kings who sits on His throne in heaven and His kingdom is perpetual forever, whereas all the peoples of the world are passing away and their power is temporary; rather, He uses them to carry out His will.

5.19.0.en: The people of God entreat Him not to leave them long under this discipline and humiliation under the hand of Babylon, and from the length of the period and the severity of the discipline they felt that it was a long time, so they entreated God to remove the punishment from them.

5.20.0.en: In hope the people ask God to bring them back to Him and renew their life in Him, so they return and worship Him in purity, for their return from captivity is a return to the worship of God in His temple, that is, it is a spiritual return and not a return to possessing lands and material good things.

5.21.0.en: The people of God ask from the depth of tribulation, and protest to God that He should reject them utterly and be angry with them forever, because He is their merciful and tender Father.

5.21.1.en: Entreat God in all your needs and trust that He loves you and wants to remove every tribulation from you, but He waits for your faith and your love for Him, which appears in the persistence of prayer.

5.21.3.en: 1- Jeremiah is a Hebrew word meaning "God establishes" or "God repairs," and the name of the prophet indicates the purpose of his ministry, for he will root out, pull down, build and plant (Jer 1:10).

5.21.4.en: 2- Jeremiah was born in the village of Anathoth, which lies northeast of Jerusalem at a distance of three miles, and it is a village set apart for the dwelling of priests (Josh 21:18). Jeremiah was of priestly descent, and his great forefather was Abiathar, who was high priest with Zadok in the days of David the prophet. Jeremiah was a priest and a prophet, but he focused his ministry on prophecy and not on the priesthood.

5.21.5.en: 3- Jeremiah was born in 646 BC at the end of the reign of Manasseh king of Judah, and in his childhood and youth he was a contemporary of Josiah, the righteous king. Because Josiah did not begin his reforms until eighteen years after he became king, Jeremiah saw corruption surrounding him on every side, which troubled him greatly, since he loved God.

5.21.6.en: 4- Jeremiah was influenced by the prophets before him, who confronted corruption with strong prophecies, such as Isaiah, Zephaniah, Hosea and Obadiah.

5.21.7.en: 5- Jeremiah was tender in feeling and a lover of God, so he felt God's distress and wrath at the evils of his people. God called him while he was a young man to proclaim His prophecies, and he began his prophecies when he was twenty years old, and that was in the thirteenth year of Josiah, that is, in 626 BC. Josiah had not yet begun his religious reforms. Thus Jeremiah, by his prophecies, was an encouragement to Josiah to begin his reforms by destroying the idols and restoring prayer to the temple of God.

5.21.8.en: 6- When God called Jeremiah to the ministry of prophecy, he excused himself and pleaded that he was young and unable to perform this ministry, but God encouraged him, so he rose and began his ministry (Jer 1:5-7).

5.21.9.en: 7- Jeremiah prophesied, and rebuked all classes of the people for their sins: the king, the chiefs, the teachers, the prophets, the scribes and the people at large, that they might repent.

5.21.10.en: 8- Jeremiah loved virginity, then God commanded him to it so that he might be an illustrative image for the people, because there would be no stability, since captivity was coming, and therefore there was no opportunity for marriage and begetting children (Jer 16:2). All this was so that they might turn back from the worship of idols and their evil lust.

5.21.12.en: 9- After Jeremiah had gone on with his prophecies, and Josiah with his reforms, Hilkiah the high priest found a copy of the Law in the temple, and when Josiah read it he was deeply moved and tore his clothes, and Josiah consulted Huldah the prophetess, who declared God's wrath upon the people and that He would punish them with captivity, but because of Josiah's humbling himself this would come after his death. So the prophecies of Huldah confirmed the prophecies of Jeremiah, which encouraged Jeremiah to continue his rebuke and his call of his people to repentance (2 Chr 34:22).

5.21.13.en: 10- King Josiah kept the Passover, and called to it not only the inhabitants of his kingdom Judah but also those remaining of the twelve tribes, who had been taken captive by the kingdom of Assyria, and Jeremiah rejoiced at the people's return to God at this great celebration.

5.21.14.en: 11- Jeremiah continued his rebuke of the people, but they rejected his prophecies, relying on the beginning of the decline and weakness of the kingdom of Assyria, which ruled the world and enslaved them. They saw that there was no danger to them, so they did not fear or obey God through the mouth of Jeremiah, and did not believe that their city would be ruined, and likewise their temple, forgetting that God is able to permit its destruction at the hand of any man, as happened at the hand of Babylon.

5.21.15.en: 12- When Jeremiah reached the age of thirty-seven, Necho king of Egypt killed King Josiah (2 Chr 35:20-24), and his son Jehoahaz became king. He was weak and young, and sadly he restored the worship of idols. So Necho king of Egypt took him captive, and made Jehoiakim his brother king in his place. Jehoiakim was also wicked, and continued in idol worship. All this troubled Jeremiah, but he continued his prophecies and his call of the people to repentance.

5.21.16.en: 13- Jeremiah warned King Jehoiakim to repent and walk like his father Josiah, but he did not obey him. And Jeremiah proclaimed his prophecies at the gate of the house of the Lord to all the people, that God was calling them to repentance and that captivity was coming upon them. But the people did not repent, and the false prophets deceived them (Jer 20:1, 2) that they would have peace, and the priests helped them in this evil.

5.21.17.en: 14- They seized Jeremiah and imprisoned him, and Jeremiah thought of not continuing his prophecies, but the word of God was like fire within him, so he returned to prophesy, and God supported him and strengthened him (Jer 20:7-9). The life of Jeremiah

5.21.18.en: 15- The priests prevented Jeremiah from entering the temple, so he dictated his prophecies to Baruch the prophet, who read them at the gate of the house of the Lord and to the chiefs. And they informed the king, who was angry and burned the prophecies (Jer 36:20-26), so Jeremiah dictated them a second time, and Baruch wrote them, and after this Jeremiah and Baruch remained in hiding, because the king wanted to kill them (Jer 22:19).

5.21.19.en: 16- King Jehoiakim died and his corpse was cast on the ground like a donkey, as Jeremiah prophesied (Jer 22:19). And his son Jehoiachin reigned for three months, then the king of Babylon took him captive and made his uncle Zedekiah king in his place (2 Chr 36:9, 10). He was weak in character, at times showing submission to Jeremiah, then turning against him after this through submission to the wicked chiefs of Judah. Jeremiah had reached the age of 48 when Zedekiah became king.

5.21.20.en: 17- After four years of Zedekiah's reign he rebelled against the king of Babylon, so the king of Babylon summoned him and rebuked him, and he was very afraid.

5.21.21.en: 18- The wicked chiefs of Judah rose against Jeremiah and imprisoned him in a harsh prison, and some time after this Zedekiah moved him to a less harsh prison, as he wanted to hear some counsels from him (Jer 37:18-21). And after Jeremiah was brought out he was imprisoned again in a harsh prison, and one of the few pious chiefs interceded, so they brought him out (Jer 38:7-12). Jeremiah bore all this with wonderful patience, but continued in courage to proclaim the prophecies of God that the Babylonian captivity was coming upon them and that they must repent.

5.21.22.en: 19- Jeremiah was a contemporary of other prophets who prophesied the word of God and called the people to repentance, such as Habakkuk the prophet and Urijah the prophet, who prophesied in the land of Judah, which encouraged Jeremiah, and likewise Ezekiel the prophet prophesied in Babylon with prophecies that confirm the prophecies of Jeremiah; all these prophecies were warnings from God that the people might repent.

5.21.23.en: 20- The king of Babylon besieged Jerusalem several times after attacking the land of Judea, and in the end Jerusalem fell into the hand of Babylon, and he burned her and her temple (Jer 34), and that was in 587 BC. Jeremiah's age at that time was 59, and Zedekiah fled, but the men of Babylon seized him and his sons and killed them The life of Jeremiah Nebuchadnezzar before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah's eyes and sent him to Babylon to be imprisoned there (2 Kgs 25:4-6).

5.21.24.en: 21- Jeremiah remained in Jerusalem and was like a tender father weeping over his people, and he wrote the Book of Lamentations known by his name. And he called the people to repentance and submission to Babylon and not to seek shelter in Egypt, but they did not obey him and went to Egypt, and even carried him against his will to Egypt.

5.21.25.en: 22- Jeremiah continued to call his people in Egypt to repent and not to worship the idols of Egypt and to submit to Babylon, which would attack Egypt, so the Jews were troubled by him and rose against him and stoned him, and he was martyred in Egypt after reaching the age of 60, having prophesied to his people for more than 40 years.

5.21.26.en: 23- Jeremiah was a symbol of Christ, who came to His own and His own received Him not (Jn 1:11), and he bore sufferings to death, like Christ, so he died at the hand of his people whom he had shepherded throughout his life.
